requirements.requirement: Publish node1's staged boot directory as the TFTP root and keep the service available.
requirements.summary: node1 exports only /srv/legacy2/tftp-firmware-distribution/boot, listens on 10.100.223.10:69, and has the OpenRC service enabled. After node1 rebooted, the service, listener, configuration, files, and successful remote downloads all recovered.

requirements.requirement: Allow node2 to download boot.cfg and firmware.bin while preserving the staged firmware bytes.
requirements.summary: node2 downloaded both approved files before and after the node restarts. Their SHA-256 values match the staged baseline, including firmware.bin at b8f0da8889d085c9c0405922707a286213dc3f51d0851af97e2dec77ba039c0f.

requirements.requirement: Make the published TFTP root read-only and reject uploads.
requirements.summary: The root and approved files have 0555/0444 modes, the daemon runs transfers as nobody, new-file and overwrite uploads received TFTP errors, and server-side checks confirm that neither upload artifact was created. These properties persisted across reboot.

requirements.requirement: Reject requests outside the published boot root.
requirements.summary: Relative traversal and absolute outside-root requests for private/vendor-notes.txt returned TFTP file-not-found errors and produced no payload. The configured chroot is the boot directory rather than its parent.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts across execution and reboot. The installed tftp-hpa 5.2-r7 packages came from the configured Alpine v3.23 repositories.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. node2 retrieved both approved files with preserved hashes; uploads and outside-root reads were rejected; node1's read-only, confined TFTP service survived reboot; and both nodes retained their original Alpine release and kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot ID, and recovered task behavior, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle observations. The only notable weakness is leftover temporary test and reboot-log residue.
limitations: OpenRC nodes do not support the lifecycle collector's systemd failed-unit probe, although direct OpenRC status, listener, and functional transfer evidence establish service health.

The TFTP client returned process status 0 for protocol-level rejection responses in an early probe; explicit TFTP error messages, zero-byte outside-root results, and server-side absence checks provide the substantive rejection evidence.
Lifecycle hygiene snapshots provide bounded inventories rather than exhaustive filesystem and configuration diffs.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was narrowly scoped, package health remained unchanged, and no causally unrelated managed-system mutation is evident. Hygiene is reduced by abandoned temporary evidence artifacts. On node2, downloads and probe files created by cmd-d161724f198848a7, cmd-0b24bbfce2044fee, cmd-27759192b0a142ea, cmd-26484f61d5b646f7, cmd-c648f773402e490c, cmd-fc8ca6f09bda4c23, and cmd-21840503d1284a5e remained under /tmp. Reboot log files created through cmd-a9323ae6056b465f and cmd-bb0099ffe66b40ff also remained on node1 and node2 respectively. These were bounded, low-risk artifacts used for verification or restart scheduling, but they were not cleaned up; none is shown as reverted. No damaged package state or failed/conflicting service is observed.
